question: An AI research team is developing a natural language processing model that relies on several open-source libraries. Which of the following is the team's BEST course of action to ensure the integrity of the software packages used? A. Maintain a list of frequently used libraries to ensure consistent application in projects. B. Retrain the model regularly to handle package and library updates. C. Scan the packages and libraries for malware prior to installation. D. Use the latest version of all libraries from public repositories.

An organization plans to apply an AI system to its business, but developers find it difficult to predict system results due to lack of visibility to the inner workings of the AI model. Which of the following is the GREATEST challenge associated with this situation? A. Assigning a risk owner who is responsible for system uptime and performance B. Continuing operations to meet expected AI security requirements C. Determining average turnaround time for AI transaction completion D. Gaining the trust of end users through explainability and transparency
Which of the following is MOST important to consider when validating a third-party AI tool? A. Terms and conditions B. Roundtable testing C. Right to audit D. Industry analysis and certifications

After implementing a third-party generative AI tool, an organization learns about new regulations related to how organizations use AI. Which of the following would be the BEST justification for the organization to decide not to comply? A. The AI tool is widely used within the industry. B. The AI tool is regularly audited. C. The risk is within the organization's risk appetite. D. The cost of noncompliance was not determined.
Which of the following is the MOST important consideration when deciding how to compose an AI red team? A. Resource availability B. Time-to-market constraints C. Skills matrix D. AI use cases

An organization's CIO provided the AI steering committee with a list of AI technologies in use and tasked them with categorizing the technologies by risk. Which of the following should the committee do FIRST? A. Begin grouping similar AI products and solutions together. B. Ensure the AI technologies are included in the asset inventory. C. Assess risk levels based on risk appetite and regulatory requirements. D. Identify vulnerabilities related to the technologies in use.

A large pharmaceutical company using a new AI solution to develop treatment regimens is concerned about potential hallucinations with the introduction of real-world data. Which of the following is MOST likely to reduce this risk? A. Penetration testing B. Data asset validation C. Human-in-the-loop D. AI impact analysis

Which of the following should be the PRIMARY consideration for an organization concerned about liabilities associated with unforeseen behavior from agentic AI systems? A. Model dependencies B. Approved base models C. Acceptable risk level D. Accountability model

During the creation of a new large language model (LLM), an organization procured training data from multiple sources. Which of the following is MOST likely to address the CISO's security and privacy concerns? A. Data minimization B. Data augmentation C. Data classification D. Data discovery

An organization is reviewing an AI application to determine whether it is still needed. Engineers have been asked to analyze the number of incorrect predictions against the total number of predictions made. Which of the following is this an example of? A. Model validation B. Control self-assessment (CSA) C. Explainable decision-making D. Key performance indicator (KPI)

Which of the following is the MOST critical key risk indicator (KRI) for an AI system? A. The amount of data in the model B. The rate of drift in the model C. The accuracy rate of the model D. The response time of the model

How can an organization BEST protect itself from payment diversions caused by deepfake attacks impersonating management? A. Require mandatory deepfake detection training for all employees. B. Implement resilient payment approval processes. C. Mandate that payments be sent only once per week. D. Issue a security policy on deepfakes.
Which of the following technologies can be used to manage deepfake risk? A. Adaptive authentication B. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) C. Systematic data tagging D. Blockchain

An organization is facing a deepfake attack intended to manipulate stock prices. The organization's crisis communication plan has been activated. Which of the following is MOST important to include in the initial response? A. Engage with brand monitoring services to track social media activity. B. Conduct a detailed forensic analysis to identify the source of the deepfake. C. Provide clarifying information in a pre-approved public statement. D. Conduct employee awareness training on recognizing deepfake videos and audio.

Which of the following BEST reduces the risk of exposing sensitive data through the output of large language models (LLMs) in applications? A. Enforcing least privilege access B. Conducting adversarial testing C. Encrypting data in transit and at rest D. Implementing data sanitization techniques

Which of the following would BEST help to prevent the compromise of a facial recognition AI system through the use of alterations in facial appearance? A. Enhancing training data to increase variance B. Fine-tuning the AI model to decrease hallucinations C. Monitoring the system for misuse cases D. Implementing a secondary AI system to confirm images

An organization concerned about the ethical and responsible use of a newly developed AI product should consider implementing: A. model cards. B. security by design. C. vendor monitoring. D. an accountability model.
Which of the following metrics BEST evaluates the ability of a model to correctly identify all true positive instances? A. F1 score B. Specificity C. Precision D. Recall

The PRIMARY reason to conduct a privacy impact assessment (PIA) on an AI system is to: A. identify applicable regulations. B. determine whether personal data is poisoned. C. build customer confidence. D. analyze how personal data is handled.

Which of the following will BEST reduce data bias in machine learning (ML) algorithms? A. Utilizing unstructured data sets B. Adopting a more simplified model C. Diversifying the model training data D. Securing the model training data

Which of the following should be done FIRST when developing an acceptable use policy for generative AI? A. Consult with risk management and legal. B. Review AI regulatory requirements. C. Determine the scope and intended use of AI. D. Review existing company policies.

A large language model (LLM) has been manipulated to provide advice that serves an attacker's objectives. Which of the following attack types does this situation represent? A. Data poisoning B. Evasion attack C. Privilege escalation D. Model inversion

From a risk perspective, which of the following is the MOST important step when implementing an adoption strategy for AI systems? A. Establishing a comprehensive AI risk assessment framework B. Implementing a robust risk analysis methodology tailored to AI-specific tasks C. Conducting an AI risk assessment and updating the enterprise risk register D. Benchmarking against peer organizations' AI risk strategies

Which of the following is MOST important to monitor in order to ensure the effectiveness of an organization's AI vendor management program? A. Vendor results in compliance training programs B. Vendor participation in industry AI research C. Vendor reviews of external AI threat reports D. Vendor compliance with AI-related requirements

After deployment, an AI model's output begins to drift outside of the expected range. Which of the following is the development team's BEST course of action? A. Return to an earlier phase in the AI life cycle. B. Take the AI model offline. C. Adjust the hyperparameters of the AI model. D. Create an emergency change request to correct the issue.

The PRIMARY ethical concern of generative AI is that it may: A. cause information integrity issues. B. cause information to become unavailable. C. breach the confidentiality of information. D. produce unexpected data that could lead to bias.

Which of the following is the MOST effective use of AI-enabled tools in a security operations center (SOC)? A. Employing AI-enabled tools to reduce false negatives by detecting subtle attack patterns B. Replacing human analysis with automated AI decision-making processes C. Assigning AI-enabled tools to triage non-critical alerts to preserve SOC resources D. Using AI-enabled tools exclusively to classify all types of security incidents

Which of the following recommendations would BEST help a service provider mitigate the risk of lawsuits arising from generative AI's access to and use of internet data? A. Review log information that records how data was collected. B. Disclose service provider policies to declare compliance with regulations. C. Activate filtering logic to exclude intellectual property flags. D. Appoint a data steward specialized in AI to strengthen security governance.
Which of the following types of testing can MOST effectively mitigate prompt hacking? A. Adversarial B. Input C. Load D. Regression

An organization recently introduced a generative AI chatbot that can interact with users and answer their queries. Which of the following would BEST mitigate hallucination risk identified by the risk team? A. Performing model testing and validation B. Ensuring model developers have been trained in AI risk C. Fine-tuning the foundational model D. Training the foundational model on large data sets

An organization plans to implement a new AI system. Which of the following is the MOST important factor in determining the level of risk monitoring activities required? A. The organization's risk appetite B. The organization's risk tolerance C. The organization's number of AI system users D. The organization's compensating controls

Which of the following employee awareness topics would MOST likely be revised to account for AI-enabled cyber risk? A. Malicious insider threats B. Clean desk policy C. Authentication controls D. Social engineering

Which of the following BEST ensures the integrity of data sets used to train AI models? A. Collection and retention of only necessary data sets B. Tracking and verification of data sets via cryptographic controls C. Clear documentation of data sources, types used, and processing steps D. Appropriate storage of data sets according to documented classification processes

Which of the following BEST describes the role of risk documentation in an AI governance program? A. Offering detailed analyses of technical risk and vulnerabilities B. Demonstrating governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) for external stakeholders C. Outlining the acceptable levels of risk for AI-related initiatives D. Providing a record of past AI-related incidents for audits

Which of the following AI system vulnerabilities is MOST easily exploited by adversaries? A. Weak controls for access to the AI model B. Lack of protection against denial of service (DoS) attacks C. Inaccurate generalizations from new data by the AI model D. Inability to detect input modifications causing inappropriate AI outputs

Which of the following is the BEST approach for minimizing risk when integrating acceptable use policies for AI foundation models into business operations? A. Rely on the developer's enforcement mechanisms. B. Implement responsible development training and awareness. C. Establish AI model life cycle policy and procedures. D. Limit model usage to predefined scenarios specified by the developer.

Which of the following key risk indicators (KRIs) is MOST relevant when evaluating the effectiveness of an organization's AI risk management program? A. Percentage of critical business systems with AI components B. Number of AI-related training requests submitted C. Number of AI models deployed into production D. Percentage of AI project in compliance

Which of the following AI-driven systems should have the MOST stringent recovery time objective (RTO)? A. Health support system B. Credit risk modeling system C. Car navigation system D. Industrial control system

An organization has requested a developer to apply AI algorithms to existing modules in order to improve customer service quality. At this stage, which of the following should be considered FIRST? A. IT management may need to revise the service agreement if AI behavior cannot be predefined. B. The organization may need to explain the performance of the applied AI algorithm. C. Project sponsors may need to agree on a phased approach in order to ensure safe release. D. The developer may need to be held accountable for business inquiries raised by customers.

Which of the following BEST describes how supervised learning models help reduce false positives in cybersecurity threat detection? A. They dynamically generate new labeled data sets. B. They analyze patterns in data to group legitimate activity from actual threats. C. They learn from historical labeled data. D. They use real-time feature engineering to automatically adjust decision boundaries.
When an attacker uses synthetic data to reverse engineer an organization's AI model, it is an example of which of the following types of attack? A. Prompt B. Poisoning C. Distillation D. Inversion

Which of the following is the GREATEST benefit of implementing an AI tool to safeguard sensitive data and prevent unauthorized access? A. Timely initiation of incident response B. Reduced number of false positives C. Timely analysis of endpoint activities D. Reduced need for data classification

Which of the following is the MOST important course of action prior to placing an in-house developed AI solution into production? A. Deploy a prototype of the solution. B. Perform a privacy, security, and compliance gap analysis. C. Obtain senior management sign-off. D. Perform testing, evaluation, validation, and verification.

Which of the following BEST represents a combination of quantitative and qualitative metrics that can be used to comprehensively evaluate AI transparency? A. AI explainability reports and bias metrics B. AI system availability and downtime metrics C. AI ethical impact and user feedback metrics D. AI model complexity and accuracy metrics

A retail organization implements an AI-driven recommendation system that utilizes customer purchase history. Which of the following is the BEST way for the organization to ensure privacy and comply with regulatory standards? A. Establishing a governance committee to oversee AI privacy practices B. Storing customer data indefinitely to ensure the AI model has a complete history C. Maintaining a register of legal and regulatory requirements for privacy D. Conducting quarterly retraining of the AI model to maintain the accuracy of recommendations

In a new supply chain management system, AI models used by participating parties are interactively connected to generate advice in support of management decision making. Which of the following is the GREATEST challenge related to this architecture? A. Explaining the overall benefit of the system to stakeholders B. Establishing clear lines of responsibility for AI model outputs C. Identifying hallucinations returned by AI models D. Determining the aggregate risk of the system

When integrating AI for innovation, which of the following can BEST help an organization manage security risk? A. Evaluating compliance requirements B. Re-evaluating the risk appetite C. Adopting a phased approach D. Seeking third-party advice
A model producing contradictory outputs based on highly similar inputs MOST likely indicates the presence of: A. evasion attacks. B. poisoning attacks. C. membership inference. D. model exfiltration.

Which of the following is the MOST serious consequence of an AI system correctly guessing the personal information of individuals and drawing conclusions based on that information? A. The exposure of personal information may result in litigation. B. The exposure of personal information may lead to a decline in public trust. C. The publicly available output of the model may include false or defamatory statements about individuals. D. The output may reveal information about individuals or groups without their knowledge.

An organization is adopting an agentic AI solution from an external vendor to support its internal IT operations. To evaluate the security posture of this system, which of the following provides the MOST reliable and independently verifiable evidence of implemented security controls? A. Industry benchmarking peer review B. Third-party audit reports C. Internal red team testing reports D. General AI security whitepapers

The PRIMARY goal of data poisoning attacks is to: A. undermine the integrity of the AI system's outputs. B. manipulate the behavior of the model during development. C. compromise the confidentiality of model input data. D. compromise the confidentiality of output data from the model.

An organization is planning to commission a third-party AI system to make decisions using sensitive data. Which of the following metrics is MOST important for the organization to consider? A. Accessibility rating B. Model response time C. Accuracy thresholds D. Service availability

Which of the following is the MOST effective way to prevent a model inversion attack? A. Monitor model output for anomalous patterns. B. Utilize data pseudonymization techniques. C. Implement differential privacy during model training. D. Ensure data minimization best practices.

Which of the following is the BEST way to ensure role clarity and staff effectiveness when implementing AI-assisted security monitoring tools? A. Defer implementation until the security team can be expanded with data scientists. B. Increase training budgets for business staff to obtain vendor-neutral AI certifications. C. Update the security program to include cross-functional AI-specific responsibilities. D. Transition responsibilities for AI tools to external consultants for improved scalability.

A CISO has been tasked with providing key performance indicators (KPIs) on the organization's newly launched AI chatbot. Which of the following are the BEST metrics for the CISO to recommend? A. Response time and throughput B. Error rate and bias detection C. Customer effort score and user retention rate D. Explainability and F1 score

A global organization has experienced multiple incidents of staff copying confidential data into public chatbots and acting on the model outputs. Which of the following is MOST important to reduce short-term risk when launching an AI security awareness initiative? A. Delivering role-based and scenario-driven AI security training mapped to policy and job functions B. Requiring employees to complete an annual generic phishing and deepfake awareness module C. Publishing an AI acceptable use policy and collecting e-signatures of employees D. Blocking access to public large language models (LLMs) at the network perimeter

When robust input controls are not practical on a large language model (LLM) to prevent prompt injection attacks from external threats, which of the following would be the BEST compensating control to address the risk? A. Fine-tune the system to validate the AI system's inputs. B. Implement identity and access management (IAM). C. Conduct human reviews of the AI system's inputs. D. Review and annotate the AI system's outputs.

An AI system that supports critical processes has deviated from its expected performance, resulting in biased outcomes. Which of the following is the BEST course of action? A. Activate the model kill switch. B. Conduct audits of the data and model. C. Perform a root cause analysis to identify mitigation steps. D. Retrain the model with a new and diverse data set.

To ensure the ethical and responsible use of AI, which of the following AI usage policy metrics is MOST important for an organization to monitor? A. Number of reported policy violations B. Number of AI projects that have undergone policy compliance review C. Frequency of policy consultations by employees D. Frequency of policy reviews and updates

Which of the following is the PRIMARY purpose of a dedicated AI management system policy? A. Ensuring environmental impact is minimized B. Optimizing AI model accuracy C. Complying with external regulations D. Providing a framework to set AI objectives
Which of the following AI data life cycle phases presents the GREATEST inherent risk? A. Monitoring B. Maintenance C. Preparation D. Training

Which of the following should be the MOST important consideration when conducting an AI impact assessment? A. Achieve business objectives B. Effect on employee retention C. Security awareness training D. Reputation of the organization

When selecting an AI model for a life insurance organization to enhance fraud detection, which factor is MOST critical to ensure secure and reliable deployment? A. Robustness B. Accuracy C. Explainability D. Adaptability

An organization is considering a Software as a Service (SaaS)-based HR system that uses AI to automate resume vetting and pre-screening of candidates. Which of the following controls is MOST important to review? A. Inclusion of diverse and representative training data B. Availability of data backups to all customers C. Periodic conformity assessments performed by the vendor D. Encryption and isolation of data from other customers

Within an incident handling process, which of the following would BEST help restore end user trust with an AI system? A. Remediation of the AI system based on lessons learned. B. The AI model's outputs are validated by team members. C. AI is being used to monitor incident detection and alerts. D. The AI model prioritizes incidents based on business impact.

Which of the following is the MOST important consideration when an organization is adopting generative AI for personalized advertising? A. Fraud risk B. Reputational risk C. Commercial risk D. Regulatory risk

Which of the following BEST describes the role of transparency in AI? A. Publishing AI mechanisms, data sources, and decision-making processes while making them openly available B. Persuading someone that the AI tool in use is beneficial and operates as expected C. Talking through a decision tree to better understand how the algorithm made each of its choices D. Explaining the AI system in an understandable and logical way so reasons for decisions can be given

A model stealing attack has been launched on an AI system that has been in use for two years. Which of the following would BEST mitigate the impact of the attack? A. Regularly monitoring AI systems for suspicious activities B. Replacing the AI model with a new model that hides confidence levels C. Implementing strict access controls to the model's architecture D. Updating the deployed training data with new adversarial data

Which of the following is the MOST effective way to detect data poisoning in generative AI models? A. Evaluating data normalization integrity before model training B. Evaluating model outputs using external benchmarks to measure consistency C. Monitoring the frequency of anomalous patterns in the training data D. Analyzing model performance by comparing outputs before and after updates

Which of the following is the MOST effective and secure way to prevent model attribute attacks against an organization's centralized AI system training data that includes sensitive information about individuals? A. Monitoring the output of AI learning models continuously B. Using federated learning to train AI algorithms C. Implementing a cross-validation AI learning model D. Removing private data from AI training datasets

Which of the following AI system use cases would present the GREATEST regulatory compliance risk for an organization expanding into foreign markets? A. Employee performance ranking B. Personalized marketing recommendations C. Email spam filtering D. Customer support chatbots
Which of the following is the BEST mechanism for identifying risk associated with the output of an AI application? A. Internal testing B. Direct feedback C. Data analytics D. Data provenance

When deploying an AI system, which of the following actions is MOST important to ensure the tradeoffs of performance and accuracy are appropriately considered? A. Monitoring key risk indicators (KRIs) against risk tolerance B. Aligning risk tolerance to key performance indicators (KPIs) C. Testing the system's technical controls D. Realigning organizational goals to the system

An organization's HR chatbot was discovered generating fake employee details using a third-party API. Which would be the information security team's BEST recommendation? A. Retrain the chatbot to validate input. B. Limit the chatbot's communication with the third-party API. C. Review the chatbot's test reports. D. Request the third-party API logs for review.

After implementing generative AI tools, an organization was notified of new critical compliance requirements aimed at verifying how AI is being used. Which of the following should be done FIRST? A. Create a policy for responsible use. B. Schedule regular compliance reviews. C. Develop a report of control compliance. D. Define access control rules.

An AI system sponsored by an organization has expanded by connecting with an increased number of third-party systems. Which of the following would be an information security manager's BEST recommendation in this situation? A. Monitor server utilization to reach the optimal operational state. B. Define clear lines of accountability for control ownership. C. Conduct due diligence on new third-party contracts. D. Introduce cost distribution methods that are fair to all third parties.

Which of the following is BEST to review in order to detect issues related to data used throughout an AI system's life cycle? A. Data quality requirements B. User access logs C. Data retention policies D. Data flow diagrams

An organization lacks visibility into the decision-making processes of a newly deployed AI model, and there are concerns regarding accuracy, bias, and stakeholder trust. Which of the following is the BEST way to improve model accuracy? A. Implement a governance system that defines procedures for model testing and validation. B. Establish monitoring controls to track AI decision-making and escalate anomalies for further analysis. C. Increase the size of training datasets to encompass as many various scenarios as possible. D. Require explainability features and review of AI outputs as part of model governance.

An organization uses an AI model to optimize traffic signals and predict congestion. Due to misconfiguration and lack of validation, the system over-prioritizes low-traffic areas, causing gridlock in major cities. Which of the following should be done FIRST to address this issue? A. Retrain the model in real time using new traffic data. B. Roll back the AI system to a previous version. C. Continue running the AI model and deploy a secondary system. D. Disable the AI system and issue a public statement.

Which of the following is the MOST important reason to establish AI-specific key risk indicators (KRIs)? A. Explainability and transparency deficiencies can be more quickly identified. B. AI systems learn and change as they interact with dynamic environments. C. Continuous availability is more critical for AI systems than for traditional systems. D. KRIs help to identify potential threats that may exploit AI system vulnerabilities.

An attacker used model poisoning to insert a backdoor into an open-source AI model, causing a data breach. Which of the following is the FIRST action to prevent reoccurrence? A. Isolate the AI system, retrain the source model, and secure the data pipelines. B. Implement a security orchestration, automation, and response (SOAR) solution. C. Perform a root cause analysis, secure the supply chain, and validate model outputs. D. Engage legal counsel, implement regulatory monitoring, and update the response plan.

A bank's fraud detection AI model is trained on customer transaction data. A customer submits a data erasure request under privacy law, but the data also exists in training sets. Which of the following is the BEST approach if there is concern that complete data removal may reduce accuracy? A. Deny the request because legitimate purpose of use outweighs privacy rights. B. Suspend the AI model until all erasure requests have been processed. B. Update standard operating procedures to ensure that the customer's data is fully deleted. C. Inform the customer that deletion from AI models is technically infeasible.

When developing organizational generative AI policies, the FIRST step is to: A. understand how the organization intends to ethically use generative AI. B. adopt current AI legal and regulatory requirements. C. identify potential risk associated with the deployment of generative AI. D. inventory the current state of AI systems, use cases, and processes.

Which of the following is the BEST approach for improving the robustness of an AI system in production? A. Reducing model complexity to simplify inference and minimize computational errors B. Encrypting training datasets to protect against data theft C. Limiting user access to the AI system to prevent misuse D. Implementing automated retraining to handle drift and performance degradation
Which of the following processes involves tagging and labeling raw datasets to create training data sets? A. Categorization B. Transformation C. Annotation D. Classification

An organization is implementing a large language model (LLM) to answer questions for both employees and customers. The CIO wants the LLM to provide employees with additional internal data that should not be shared with customers. Which of the following is the MOST secure approach? A. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with access control lists (ACLs) B. Model fine tuning with increased use of function calls C. Prompt sanitization D. Allow list employee access

A bank is training an AI credit scoring model on a vast amount of sensitive customer data. Which of the following is the MOST critical security risk in this training process? A. Data poisoning to corrupt training outcomes B. Algorithmic bias leading to discriminatory lending C. Resources needed to retrain and validate the AI model D. Model inversion or membership inference attacks

A pharmaceutical organization uses an AI solution from a third-party vendor to analyze confidential research and development data. Which of the following controls is MOST essential to ensure the vendor's AI solution complies with the organization's security requirements? A. Communicate security requirements to the vendor. B. Minimize sensitive data being used by the vendor's AI solution. C. Implement a private instance of the solution. D. Review the vendor's independent security audit report.

To facilitate the adoption of a new AI system, an organization has provided data access to third-party solutions. Which of the following BEST mitigates risk associated with third-party software? A. Updating tolerance levels to accept new risk B. Designating boundaries for AI operation C. Consulting AI experts to help mitigate the risk D. Conducting regular external audits

Which of the following would BEST ensure safe implementation of AI systems? A. Selection of AI projects that align with business objectives. B. Compliance with the AI risk management framework and applicable regulations. C. Establishment of an AI program steering committee to govern AI implementation. D. Phased implementation with human-in-the-loop validation before full rollout.

Which of the following is the MOST effective way to identify deepfakes generated by AI? A. Examining irregularities in metadata or data traces B. Detecting irregular pixel patterns or distorted frames C. Analyzing biometric inconsistencies D. Comparing the model card to the output generated by AI

Which of the following is the GREATEST benefit of using agentic AI in security operations? A. Enabling automatic responses for security incidents B. Minimizing awareness training needs C. Reducing the level of resources required for human monitoring D. Reducing the number of false positives
